# GPU and hardware support {#sec-gpu}

- Let users control which hardware greta runs on. Grouping label: the
  `hardware` cluster. Small and self-contained - the theme that remains
  once the installation and unpin work moved into milestone 1.
- Nothing here blocks anything else, and nothing else blocks it. The
  milestone can move in the schedule freely, which is why it is the
  natural candidate to trade against adaptive sampling.

**The shape of the work.** greta currently gives the user no say in
device placement: TensorFlow picks, and greta neither reports nor
overrides the choice. The three issues below are one feature ([#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545))
plus two long-standing reports that the feature would let a user
diagnose for themselves.


### [Issue #246](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/246)

- 2018-11-03
- installation
- tensorflow-cuda does not work with greta.
- problem: a CUDA-enabled TensorFlow build does not give greta GPU execution.
- finding: an eight-year-old report against TF1 and a conda install path. It cannot be judged until the unpin (milestone 1) settles which TF versions greta supports, and it cannot be *diagnosed* by a user until [#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545) gives them a way to see and set the device.
- fix: re-verify against a post-unpin TF build with a CUDA device present; if it still fails, the report becomes actionable for the first time because [#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545)'s sitrep output will say which device was selected.
- priority: low (gated on milestone 1 and [#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545)).

### [Issue #472](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/472)

- 2021-12-14
- installation
- TF installs are compiled for AVX/AVX2.
- problem: the "your CPU supports instructions this TensorFlow binary was not compiled to use" warning.
- finding: still-reproducible *upstream* behaviour - it is TensorFlow's own message about its own prebuilt wheels, not something greta emits or can suppress meaningfully. The July 2026 verification pass recorded this: "won't-fix" is a legitimate verdict here, but it is the maintainer's decision to make, not a default closure.
- fix: either suppress/contextualise the warning in greta's startup path with a pointer to what it does and does not mean for performance, or close as a deliberate won't-do. Needs a maintainer ruling, not investigation.
- priority: low (needs a decision, not code).

### [Issue #545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545)

- 2022-08-09
- (none)
- An interface to control CPU and GPU setup.
- problem: no user-facing control over, or visibility of, device placement.
- finding: this is the one real feature in the milestone, and it is what makes [#246](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/246) and [#704](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/704) tractable. It is also the reason for the minor version bump.
- fix: a session-level device interface in the spirit of `future::plan()` - a `greta_device()`-style setter plus device reporting folded into `greta_sitrep()`, so a user can both see what greta chose and override it. Build it on `with(tf$device(...))` ([#704](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/704)) rather than on environment variables.
- priority: medium (the milestone's headline).

### [Issue #704](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/704)

- 2024-08-16
- (none)
- Explore `with(tf$device())`.
- problem: greta never scopes its op construction to a device.
- finding: this is the *mechanism* for [#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545), not an independent issue. TensorFlow's device scope is the standard way to pin graph construction to a device, and greta's op construction all funnels through the dag's `define_tf` walk, which gives one obvious place to wrap.
- fix: prototype device scoping around the `define_tf` walk in `dag_class`, confirm the placement actually holds through `tf_function` tracing, then expose it as [#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545)'s implementation. Note this is a TensorFlow-specific mechanism - under the backend abstraction (milestone 8) device selection becomes something the backend contract owns, so keep the user-facing interface backend-neutral even though the first implementation is not.
- priority: medium (batches with [#545](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/545)).
